name: Museum of the Second World War
desc: The most visited museum in Poland and the reason many people come to Gdańsk. A huge underground exhibition that walks you through 1939–1945 from a Polish and European perspective — occupation, everyday life, the Holocaust, the resistance.
why: It is built UNDERGROUND, under the tilted tower. You descend and the floor shakes with bomber engines. Few museums in Europe hit this hard. Audio guide 12 zł, genuinely worth it.
tip: Sunday is NOT free (Tuesday is). Book a timed slot online the night before — weekend slots sell out. Last tickets 30 min before closing, and those cost only 17 zł.

name: European Solidarity Centre
hours: Mon, Wed–Fri 10:00–17:00 · Sat–Sun 10:00–18:00 · Tue CLOSED (technical day)
desc: The story of Solidarity, the 1980 strikes and the fall of communism, told inside the rust-coloured former shipyard building. Rooftop terrace has one of the best free views of the shipyard cranes.
why: You literally walk through the gate where Lech Wałęsa climbed the wall in 1980. The building itself (rusty steel, ship-plate textures) is an architectural landmark.
tip: The rooftop terrace and the building lobby are FREE — you only pay for exhibitions. Combine with a walk down ul. Elektryków and the 21 cranes.

name: Museum of Amber (Wielki Młyn)
desc: Baltic amber in a 14th-century mill: inclusions, 'sun stones', amber rooms, and how the amber trade built Gdańsk. Compact, beautifully lit, very photogenic.
why: Amber is Gdańsk's thing — this is the largest amber collection in Poland, in a medieval water mill. Perfect indoor filler on a cold day.
tip: GO MONDAY 26 OCT: entry is free. This is the single best free cultural deal of your trip. Arrive before 11:00 to avoid school groups.

name: Main Town Hall & Tower
hours: Mon 10:00–16:00 (free) · Tue CLOSED · Wed–Sun 10:00–16:00, Thu to 18:00
desc: Renaissance town hall with the Red Hall, gilded sculptures, and a tower view straight down ul. Długa to the Green Gate and the river.
why: The classic postcard view of Gdańsk, plus the tower clock and carillon. Free on Monday — same ticket logic as the Amber Museum.
tip: The tower is a climb, not a lift. If it is windy, the tower may close — in that case just do the Red Hall interiors.

name: The Crane (Żuraw) & Długie Pobrzeże
price: Free outside · Maritime Museum inside ~25 zł
desc: Medieval port crane with two huge wooden tread-wheels that men once walked inside to lift cargo. The whole riverside here — gates, granaries, barges — is the postcard of Gdańsk.
why: It is the largest preserved medieval port crane in Europe, and the waterfront at dusk with the lights on the water is the single most photographed spot in the city.
tip: Free to see from the quay. Walk it at blue hour (17:00–17:45 in late October) — sunset is 17:27, lights come on around 17:15.

name: St Mary's Basilica & Mariacka Street
desc: The largest brick church in the world — 30,000 people fit inside, and it took 160 years to build. Climb ~400 steps for the best rooftop panorama of the Old Town.
why: The astronomical clock does a mechanical show every day at 11:57 sharp (free, one minute). Mariacka Street outside is a cobbled canyon of amber workshops and stone terraces — the most atmospheric street in Gdańsk.
tip: Tower closes in storms — check before climbing. The 11:57 clock show is free and only takes a minute; time your visit around it.

name: Westerplatte
price: Site free · water tram 80 zł one-way / 100 zł return
desc: Where World War II in Europe began at 04:48 on 1 September 1939. Ruined barracks, the Monument to the Defenders, and a windswept peninsula between the harbour and the open sea.
why: The water tram ride there is half the attraction — you sail past the shipyards, the container terminal and the huge cranes. It is the only 'sea' experience that fits a short city break.
tip: Do it on a dry, low-wind day — this is a flat, exposed peninsula, brutally cold in wind. Monday gusts 46 km/h: take the 14:00 boat and the 16:00 back, or skip it if you feel the flight pressure.

name: Oliwa Cathedral & Organ Demonstration
price: Free entry · organ demo ~10–15 zł donation/ticket
hours: Organ demos in October: Mon–Sat 11:00 & 12:00, Sun 15:00 (20 min)
desc: A vast Cistercian cathedral with a famous 18th-century organ — 7,896 pipes, moving angels and trumpeting figures. The 20-minute demonstration is a proper 'wow' moment, not a church service.
why: The only place in Poland where the organ itself performs a mechanical theatre. It costs almost nothing and takes 20 minutes — the best value cultural experience in Gdańsk.
tip: Monday 26 Oct: demo at 11:00 AND 12:00. Get there 10:45, sit near the front centre. Then walk the Oliwa Park (free, gorgeous autumn colours) behind the cathedral.

name: Gdańsk Zoo (Oliwa)
hours: October: entry 09:00–16:00, grounds until 17:00 · open daily
desc: One of the largest zoos in Poland, set in a forested valley — giraffes, lions, elephants, and a lot of walking uphill.
why: Cheap in October (30 zł vs 45 zł in summer) and the autumn forest setting is beautiful. Only worth it if you want a nature half-day; skip if you prefer the city.
tip: It is a 15-min drive or bus from Oliwa cathedral and the terrain is hilly. Entry closes 16:00 sharp in October — go before 13:00 if you want the full loop.

name: Hevelianum & Góra Gradowa
price: Hill & fort grounds FREE · exhibitions ~30 zł
desc: A 19th-century Prussian fort on a hill 5 minutes from the Old Town, now a science centre. The grassy ramparts and the big wooden cross give a 360° panorama over the cranes, the Old Town and the harbour.
why: The best FREE sunset viewpoint in central Gdańsk, and almost no tourists. You see the whole shipyard skyline from above.
tip: Walk up from ul. Gradowa, 10 min from the flat. Take beers up for sunset at 17:27 — legal, normal, and locals do it.

name: Gdańsk Shipyard & Imperial Shipyard walk
addr: Gate No. 2, ul. Droga do Wolności
hours: Public streets 24/7 · B90/Elektryków venues Thu–Sat evenings
desc: The real, working post-industrial shipyard: 21 giant cranes, dry docks, red-brick halls, the Monument to the Fallen Shipyard Workers, and the new Imperial Shipyard development rising between them.
why: This is where the 20th century turned — and it still smells of steel and sea. Street-art, cranes and rust: the most 'Gdańsk' walk you can do, and it is free.
tip: Do it in daylight (before 16:30) — it is unlit in parts. Combine with ECS and then drinks on ul. Elektryków after 18:00.

name: Zaspa Murals
desc: A concrete housing estate covered in 60+ giant murals by international street artists — the biggest open-air gallery of its kind in Europe.
why: Completely off the tourist trail, free, and photogenic. Also a glimpse of how 90% of Poland actually lives.
tip: SKM train from Gdańsk Główny to Gdańsk Zaspa, 6 minutes, 4.80 zł. Wear comfortable shoes; the murals are spread over a big estate.

name: AmberSky Ferris Wheel
hours: Daily, roughly 11:00–20:00 — CHECK before going (closed on some days in low season)
desc: A 50-metre observation wheel on Ołowianka island, right beside the Philharmonic. Enclosed gondolas, 3 slow loops, view over the Motława, the shipyard cranes and the Old Town roofs.
why: The only way to see Gdańsk from above without climbing 400 stairs, and it is warm inside — a good 'cold hands' activity.
tip: Go at dusk (17:00) for the lights coming on. It is weather-dependent: in strong wind it stops. Book nothing in advance; just walk up.

name: Motława River Cruise
hours: Departures through the day; last boats ~17:00–18:00 in late Oct
desc: Small white boats and galleon replicas leave from the embankment for a loop around the Old Port, the shipyard and the islands.
why: Gdańsk was built by sea trade; seeing it from the water explains the whole city in an hour. Cheap, and you sit down.
tip: Boats are open-deck — pick a dry, calm day (Sat or Mon), not Sunday's 62 km/h gusts. Buy at the pier, no booking needed.

name: Axe Throwing
desc: 1.5 hours of coaching and competition with real axes, a proper instructor, and a tournament at the end. Built for groups of friends.
why: Perfect rainy-Sunday activity for five guys: competitive, indoor, no skill needed, and it ends with a winner and a lot of trash talk.
tip: Book the day before — Sunday slots fill. ~85 zł pp for 5 = ~425 zł total. Ask for pickup if the venue is outside the centre.

name: E1GOKART Indoor Karting
price: 75 zł / 8-min ride (2 rides 145 zł, 3 rides 215 zł)
desc: A proper indoor karting hall with fast electric karts, lap timing and a Grand Prix format for groups.
why: Real racing, real lap times, and a leaderboard with your names on it. The classic 'lads trip' activity, and it is indoors.
tip: Near the airport — do it on the way in or out, or combine with a taxi (18 min from the flat). 3 rides each = 215 zł pp; the 2-ride option is the sweet spot.

name: Gdańsk Shooting Centre (GCS)
addr: ul. Wrzeszcz Górny (check address on site)
price: Per round: from ~1.50 zł (.22LR) to ~5 zł (.45 ACP) + weapon rental
desc: Indoor range with pistols and rifles, instructors, and group packages. You pay per round of ammunition plus rental.
why: Poland is relaxed about sport shooting and this is a professional, safe range — a genuinely different afternoon for a group of friends.
tip: Budget ~100–150 zł pp for 30–50 rounds. Bring ID/passport — required for foreigners. Book ahead and say you are a group of 5 beginners.

name: U7 Bowling & Pool
price: Lane: 120 zł/h (Mon–Wed, Sun 17–24) · 170 zł/h (Sat 17–01) · shoes 6 zł
desc: 8 bowling lanes, 10 pool tables, darts, table football, a bar and a big screen — right under the Old Town.
why: Zero logistics, central, and handles a group of 5 perfectly: one lane, beers, pool between turns.
tip: Sunday 17:00–24:00 is 120 zł/h per lane — split 5 ways that is ~24 zł/hour each. Shoes 6 zł. Cheapest indoor fun in the centre.

name: Ergo Arena: 'Królowie Życia' concert
desc: Big Polish rock/pop show — Skawiński & Tkaczyk, '50 years on stage'. Arena holds ~10,000.
why: If you want a big-concert night instead of a bar crawl, this is the only arena show in your window. Very Polish, very loud.
tip: It clashes with your first evening. Only choose it if you land early and skip the Old Town crawl — otherwise stick to the bars.

name: Polish Baltic Philharmonic concert
hours: Sun 25/10/2026, 19:00 — Joanna Knitter & Baltic Banda 'From Hollywood to the charts'
desc: A converted 19th-century power station on the water, now one of Poland's best concert halls. Sunday's programme is film music and pop standards, not stiff classical.
why: Rainy Sunday evening, warm hall, water views, live band — a much better use of the storm than another pub.
tip: Check the site for tickets (some events sell via bilety24). Dress is smart-casual; nobody will mind jeans.

name: Pixel
desc: Gdańsk's best-known cocktail bar: dark, low ceilings, serious bartenders, long list of signature drinks.
why: The cocktails are actually good, not just strong. It is where locals take visiting friends, and it fits a group of 5 at the bar.
tip: Go early (20:00) — after 22:00 it is packed and standing. Try the smoky/whisky signatures, skip the sweet ones.

name: Cybermachina Game Pub
price: Beer ~12–16 zł · board games free with a drink
desc: Board games, retro consoles, arcade machines and craft beer. Bookshelves of games you can take to your table for free.
why: The single best bar for five friends in Gdańsk: you can actually talk, compete, and nobody cares how long you sit. Cheap.
tip: Grab a big table at the back, order a round, and ask staff to recommend a 20-minute party game. Budget ~40–60 zł pp for a long session.

name: Flisak'76
desc: Tiny, candle-lit cocktail bar on the prettiest street in the Old Town. No menu theatre, just excellent drinks.
why: Chlebnicka is 30 metres of perfect Hanseatic facades — you drink outside in the street when it is dry. Very Gdańsk.
tip: It is small: 5 people may have to stand or split. Perfect first stop of the crawl at 20:00.

name: Józef K.
desc: A long-running Piwna-street institution: wooden interior, posters, a mixed crowd of students, locals and tourists, open until the small hours.
why: Piwna is the bar street of Gdańsk and Józef K. is its living room. Cheap, unpretentious, no dress code.
tip: Great 'second stop' — after cocktails, before the club. Ask for a local craft beer on tap.

name: Winston Bar
desc: Smart little cocktail bar just off Długa with a British-club feel — dark wood, low light, proper glassware.
why: Best cocktail quality-to-crowd ratio in the centre. Good for the 'we are dressed slightly better tonight' moment.
tip: If full, Flisak'76 and Pixel are within 4 minutes' walk.

name: Pijalnia Wódki i Piwa
desc: A Polish institution: cheap vodka shots, herring and bread, communist-era decor, standing room only.
why: The authentic Polish drinking experience, at absurd prices. Five guys, five shots, five złoty each — it is a rite of passage.
tip: Order 'set' of shots + a herring snack. Do it EARLY in the night, not at 1 a.m. — pace matters.

name: Ministerstwo Śledzia i Wódki
desc: 'Ministry of Herring and Vodka' — a whole menu of cured herring preparations and flavoured vodkas, in a wood-panelled room.
why: Extremely Polish and genuinely delicious: herring five ways with ice-cold vodka. A great pre-dinner stop for five friends.
tip: Order 3–4 herring plates to share plus a vodka flight. ~45–60 zł pp. Book a table for 5 — it fills up.

name: LAbeerYNT
desc: Craft-beer bar with a rotating wall of Polish taps — IPAs, stouts, sours — and staff who actually know them.
why: Poland's craft beer scene is one of Europe's best and this is the place to taste it. Flights available.
tip: Ask for a tasting flight of 4 × 100 ml. ~25–30 zł. Sour beers here are excellent and unusual.

name: Brovarnia (brewery restaurant)
price: Mains 45–75 zł · beer brewed on site ~14 zł
desc: A brewery-restaurant in a converted granary on the water, with copper tanks visible through glass and solid Polish cooking (pierogi, duck, pork knuckle).
why: Big tables, river views, own beer, and food that soaks up the evening. The safest 'everyone will be happy' dinner for five.
tip: Book a table for 5 at 19:00 and ask for the window side. Try the wheat beer and the pork knuckle to share.

name: Cooltura club
price: Entry usually free/10 zł · drinks 12–20 zł
desc: A big multi-room club/bar with alternative, rock and electronic nights, open until 6 a.m. Student crowd, cheap drinks.
why: If the Old Town bars close at 1, this is where the night continues. Five minutes from the centre, no dress code.
tip: Go after 23:30 on Saturday. Check the event on Facebook that day — the music changes nightly.

name: Klubogaleria Bunkier
desc: A concrete bunker turned club/gallery: techno, alternative concerts, art on the walls, cigarette smoke and cheap beer.
why: The most 'underground' venue in central Gdańsk, in a genuine WWII-era shelter. For a group that wants a real night out, not a tourist bar.
tip: Check the programme first — on non-event nights it is just a bar. Saturday usually has something.

name: Ulica Elektryków (Elektryków Street)
desc: A street of bars, food trucks and clubs inside the shipyard — B90 (biggest concert club in the region), Drizzly Grizzly, W4 food hall — under giant cranes.
why: Drinking under 21 shipyard cranes at night is a Gdańsk-only experience. It is the alternative to the Old Town crawl and it is 10 minutes' walk from ECS.
tip: Saturday is the night. It is industrial and windy — wear the jacket. B90 had no show on 24/10, so check the smaller venues' socials that day.

name: Sassy / Roof Top by Sassy
desc: Rooftop bar by day with a view over the Motława, club by night with commercial house and a dressed-up crowd.
why: The only real 'rooftop + club' combo in the centre. Good for the final stop when the pub crawl needs a finish line.
tip: Saturday entry after 23:00 may have a queue and a face-control vibe. Go as a group of 5 and you will be fine.

name: Pierogarnia Mandu
desc: Gdańsk's famous pierogi restaurant: hand-folded, baked and boiled, with fillings from classic potato-cheese to duck and cherry.
why: The best pierogi in the city and the one meal everybody remembers. Portions are big, prices are fair, and it is a 10-minute walk from the flat's tram stop.
tip: Book online for 5 — walk-ins wait 30–60 min at dinner. Order 2 different kinds per person and share. Try the baked ones.

name: Bar mleczny Neptun
desc: A proper communist-era milk bar: canteen trays, laminated menu, pierogi, borscht, kotlet schabowy, kvass. Locals, pensioners, students.
why: Eating a full hot meal for 25 zł in the middle of the tourist Old Town is the best value in Gdańsk. It is also a genuine cultural experience.
tip: Order at the counter, pay at the till, collect at the hatch. Try borscht with croquettes and the plum pierogi.

name: Ryba Piła
desc: Baltic fish done simply — herring, cod, flounder, halibut — grilled or fried, with good bread and local beer.
why: You are on the Baltic; eat the fish. Less heavy than the pork-and-dumplings circuit.
tip: Ask what came in that morning. Order the fried cod and a herring starter to share.

name: 100cznia (street-food yard)
hours: In season Tue–Sun 13:00–24:00 · late Oct: limited '100cznia Inside' — CHECK before going
desc: A yard of shipping containers, food trucks, picnic tables and a stage, built on a former shipyard site. In winter it shrinks to an indoor version.
why: The best casual group lunch/dinner in Gdańsk when it is running — everyone picks their own food, no booking, cheap.
tip: It is seasonal (May–Sept full, October reduced). If closed, go to Elektryków bars or Mandu instead.

name: 107 Ogarna
desc: A narrow, brick-vaulted cocktail bar on Ogarna street with a serious drinks list and a young crowd.
why: Ogarna is the second bar street of the Old Town — less touristy than Piwna, better cocktails per złoty.
tip: Standing room only after 22:00. Good stop between Winston and Pixel.

name: Pub Lawendowa
desc: A relaxed corner pub with a small garden, pub grub and cheap draught beer — the antidote to cocktail-bar prices.
why: Where you go when the group wants to sit, eat something fried and argue about football without shouting.
tip: Kitchen closes earlier than the bar — order food before 21:00.

name: Red Light Pub
desc: A basement rock pub on Piwna: loud music, cheap beer, darts, no pretension.
why: The classic late-night Piwna stop. If you want a proper Polish 'piwnica' (cellar) night, this is it.
tip: Cash is handy. Music is loud — not the place for a deep conversation.

name: Game Over
desc: Video-game bar: consoles, PCs, retro arcades, tournaments, and beer at the table.
why: Five guys, one FIFA/Mario Kart tournament, four hours gone. Indoor, cheap, and reliably fun in bad weather.
tip: Book a console station for 5 in advance on weekends. Ask about the tournament schedule.

name: Tiki Jungle
desc: Tropical tiki bar with flaming bowls, carved wood and rum-heavy cocktails — deliberately ridiculous.
why: The one bar where ordering a giant shared bowl for five actually makes sense. Good photos, good mood.
tip: Order one 'volcano bowl' to share rather than five separate drinks — cheaper and more fun.

name: Pub Zappio
desc: A big, busy pub with sports screens, burgers and a garden — the 'watch the match' option in the centre.
why: If there is a football or rugby match on, this is where to watch it with a beer and a burger.
tip: Ask them to put the game on a specific screen; they will.

name: Mechaniczna Pomarańcza
desc: A legendary student club at Gdańsk University of Technology — cheap beer, indie/rock nights, sticky floors, zero tourists.
why: It is 10 minutes from your flat and it is where actual Gdańsk students drink. If you want a local night, this is it.
tip: Student ID gets a discount; otherwise still cheap. Best on Thursday–Saturday.

name: Pool Salon
desc: Pool hall and bar by the river with several tables, darts and a big screen.
why: Competitive, cheap, indoors, and right on the waterfront. A good pre-club or rainy-evening stop.
tip: Book a table for 5 after 19:00 — it gets busy. Winner stays on is the only fair format.

name: Brzeźno Pier & Beach
desc: A 136-metre wooden pier over the Baltic, wide sandy beach, pine trees, and a promenade of fish shacks.
why: The sea, 25 minutes from the Old Town, free. Sunset over the water with a beer from the nearby shop is the best ending to a dry day.
tip: Tram/bus from the centre ~25 min or 18 min by Uber (~35 zł). Windy and cold — take the jacket. Fish shack 'Bar Przystań' nearby for fried cod.

name: Nowy Port Lighthouse
desc: An 1894 lighthouse with a Time Ball and a view across the harbour mouth, the Westerplatte peninsula and the Baltic.
why: Industrial, off-grid, and you see the whole port from above. Pairs perfectly with Westerplatte on the same trip.
tip: Check it is open before travelling — hours shrink in late October. Combine by car with Westerplatte (5 min drive).

name: Ołowianka Island & footbridges
desc: Two little islands joined by footbridges, holding the Philharmonic, the Sołdek ship-museum, the AmberSky wheel and the Maritime Museum granaries.
why: The best short evening loop: cross the bridge, look back at the illuminated Old Town across the water, walk back over the other bridge.
tip: Do it at 17:15–17:45 for sunset + city lights. Free, flat, 25 minutes end to end.

name: SS Sołdek (museum ship)
desc: A 1949 coal-fired steamship, the first ship built entirely in Gdańsk after the war, now a museum you can walk through — engine room, hold, bridge.
why: You can climb into the engine room of a real steam ship. Kids love it, adults quietly love it more.
tip: Small and quick — 45 minutes. Combine with the Ołowianka walk and the Philharmonic.

name: Artus Court & Green Gate
price: Outside free · Artus Court interior ~20 zł
desc: The guildhall of the merchant brotherhoods, with a monumental tiled stove and ship models, plus the Green Gate that was meant to be a royal palace.
why: This is the exact centre of Hanseatic Gdańsk — the fountain, the court, the gate, all in one 100-metre square.
tip: Free to walk around outside. The Neptune Fountain in front is the meeting point everyone uses — pick it as your group rendezvous.

name: Oliwa Park (Park Oliwski)
desc: A formal French-style garden with clipped hedges, a palm house, canals and 300-year-old trees, right behind the cathedral.
why: Late-October colours, almost no tourists on a Monday morning, and it is free. The most peaceful hour you will have in Gdańsk.
tip: Enter from the cathedral side, walk the main alley to the palm house, exit towards ul. Cystersów for the tram back.

name: Sopot Pier (Molo)
price: FREE in October (paid 10 zł only 10 Apr–30 Sep)
hours: 24/7 · 20 min SKM from Gdańsk Główny (4.80 zł)
desc: The longest wooden pier in Europe — 511 metres out into the Baltic, with a marina, sailing boats and the beach on both sides.
why: It is free in your dates (the 10 zł charge ends 30 September), and the walk out over the water at sunset is the classic Tricity moment.
tip: Sunday 25 Oct is the Sopot Half Marathon — roads and the promenade are closed in the morning. Go Saturday or Monday instead.

name: Krzywy Domek & Monte Cassino
price: Free outside · Muzeum Iluzji inside ~35–45 zł
desc: The 'crooked house' — a surreal, melting building on Sopot's pedestrian main street, with shops and an illusion museum inside.
why: It is the most photographed building in Poland after the Gdańsk crane, and Monte Cassino is a good street for coffee and people-watching.
tip: Sopot is 20 min by SKM and the pier, the crooked house and the beach are all within 15 minutes' walk of each other.

name: Gdynia: ORP Błyskawica & Dar Pomorza
desc: Two floating museums side by side: a WWII destroyer that fought at Narvik, and the tall ship 'Dar Pomorza' that trained generations of Polish sailors.
why: You can walk the decks, the gun turrets and the engine rooms of a real warship. Gdynia is 25 min by SKM and feels completely different from Gdańsk.
tip: SKM Gdańsk Główny → Gdynia Główna, 25 min, ~6 zł. Both ships are 10 min walk from the station. Check Monday opening — many Gdynia museums close.

name: Malbork Castle (day trip)
price: Castle ticket ~70 zł (reduced ~45 zł) · train ~20–30 zł return
hours: Daily ~09:00–16:00 in October (last entry ~15:00) · train 40–50 min from Gdańsk Główny
desc: The largest brick castle in the world and a UNESCO site — the headquarters of the Teutonic Order, with massive walls, chapter house, and the Grand Masters' palace.
why: It is one of the great castles of Europe, 45 minutes by train, and it is the best 'big day out' if you want one. Do it only if you are happy to sacrifice a Gdańsk day.
tip: Trains from Gdańsk Główny take 40–50 min. Book the castle online — English tours sell out. It is a LOT of walking; 4–5 hours minimum. Not realistic on departure day.

name: Wisłoujście Fortress
hours: Seasonal — usually closed late Oct, CHECK before going
desc: A 17th-century fortress guarding the harbour mouth, with a circular brick tower and star-shaped earthworks.
why: Genuinely atmospheric and almost empty — but only if it is open. It pairs with Westerplatte by car.
tip: Ring ahead or check the Muzeum Gdańska site. If closed, skip it — the drive there is industrial and not worth it alone.

name: YOUR FLAT
desc: Your base: a residential street in Siedlce, 2.5 km south-west of the Old Town, 2.6 km from Gdańsk Główny station.
why: Quiet, local, cheap shops and trams on the doorstep — but not walkable to the Old Town with a hangover. Plan on tram 10/12 or a 30–40 zł Uber.
tip: Nearest tram stops: Zakopiańska (300 m) and Siedlce (600 m). Trams 10 and 12 go to the centre and to Gdańsk Główny.

name: Zakopiańska tram stop
desc: Your nearest stop, 3 minutes' walk from the flat. Trams 10 and 12 towards the centre / Gdańsk Główny.
why: This is your default way into town: 10–12 minutes to the Old Town, no parking, no traffic.
tip: Buy tickets in the Jakdojade or GoPay app (or the ticket machine on board). Validate on boarding — inspectors do fine.

name: Lewiatan supermarket
desc: The closest proper supermarket to the flat, and it is OPEN ON SUNDAY (09:00–19:00).
why: Sunday 25 October is a trading ban — Biedronka and Lidl are closed. This is your lifeline for breakfast and beers.
tip: Do a big shop Saturday evening. On Sunday use Lewiatan or the Żabka corner shops (06:00–23:00).

name: Żabka (corner shop)
desc: The Polish corner shop: cold beer, hot dogs, coffee, SIM cards, and open every day including Sunday.
why: Two minutes from the flat and open when everything else is closed. Also sells bus tickets? No — use the app.
tip: Hot dogs and coffee are actually decent. Cash and card both fine.

name: Pharmacy (Apteka)
desc: Nearest pharmacy, 4 minutes from the flat. There is also a 24-hour pharmacy in the city centre.
why: Hangover cures, plasters, cold medicine — worth knowing where it is.
tip: For anything urgent at night, search 'apteka całodobowa Gdańsk' or call 112.

name: Gdańsk Główny station
desc: The main railway station — a fairy-tale red-brick building. SKM trains to Sopot, Gdynia, the airport and Malbork leave from here.
why: Your gateway for every day trip, and the cheapest way back to the airport.
tip: SKM platforms are downstairs/underground. Buy tickets from machines or the app; validate before boarding.

name: Gdańsk Airport (GDN)
desc: Lech Wałęsa Airport, 14 km west of the city. Train station 'Gdańsk Port Lotniczy' is a 5-minute covered walk from arrivals.
why: Small, fast, and connected by train — you do not need a taxi unless you have a lot of luggage.
tip: Security is quick but the airport is busy in the evening. Be inside 90 minutes before a midnight flight.
